data.description:
## Discovered from bug 9f63 (Step 7 construct sweep)

Same defect class as 9f63 — **a persisted position advanced on "seen" rather than "done"** — but here the lost artifact is observability data rather than a work item.

`infra/scripts/observability.sh:208-212` (and the same shape at `:104`/`:107-108` replication, `:134`/`:137-138` voter, `:157`/`:158` merge-change, `:178`/`:179` deploy):

```sh
new=$((total - prev))
[ "$new" -lt 0 ] && new=$total
echo "$total" >"$offset_file"          # <-- offset advances FIRST
aws cloudwatch put-metric-data ... --value "$new" 2>/dev/null || true   # <-- may fail, silently
```

The offset file is written **before** the publish, and the publish is `2>/dev/null || true`. A transient failure (CloudWatch throttle, IMDS credential blip, network) therefore loses that interval's delta permanently: the next tick computes `total - prev` from the already-advanced baseline, so the count is never re-published.

**Loss is permanent, not self-healing** — unlike a rotation cursor, this offset excludes rather than deprioritizes.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The `voter_errors` metric is what alarms on a broken `LLM-Review` gate. So a `voter_errors` spike that happens to coincide with a CloudWatch hiccup goes un-alarmed forever — the exact "the failure is invisible" property that made 9f63 so expensive to diagnose, in the mechanism that is supposed to be watching it.

## Fix sketch

Invert the order at each of the five sites: publish first, advance the offset only when `put-metric-data` exits 0. On failure leave the offset alone so the next tick re-publishes a cumulative delta (over-reporting once is strictly safer than silently under-reporting forever).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At each of the five offset sites the offset is written only after a successful publish
- [ ] A failed publish leaves the offset unchanged, proven by a test that stubs a failing `aws` and asserts the offset file is byte-identical afterwards
- [ ] A subsequent successful publish reports the accumulated delta, not just the latest tick
data.title: observability.sh advances its metric offset before the CloudWatch publish, so a transient put-metric-data failure permanently loses that interval's count
